name: Exploiting vulnerabilities for which a patch exists (attacking non-updated software)
description: Exploiting known, already-patched vulnerabilities on systems left unpatched through lax updating or end-of-life software.
ai_shift_basis: Patch-diffing and exploit writing for known CVEs are already automated.

name: Exploiting reported but not (fully) patched vulnerabilities
description: Exploiting publicly reported vulnerabilities in the window before a patch exists or is fully applied.
ai_shift_basis: Same automation applies to partially patched vulnerabilities.

name: Finding and exploiting individual zero-days
description: Discovering or buying individual unreported vulnerabilities and exploiting them against the target's specific software or devices.
ai_shift_basis: Zero-day discovery is where AI uplift is largest (Big Sleep 2024, AIxCC 2025); capped at one tier.

name: Direct access to zero-days at scale
description: State access to a large pipeline of zero-days, e.g. via mandatory disclosure laws, enough to defeat monitoring and modest defence-in-depth.
ai_shift_basis: AI lowers the cost of a stockpile, so 'at scale' reaches lesser actors.

name: Social engineering
description: Phishing, pretexting and other deception that gets staff to reveal credentials, run attacker code, or grant access.
transcription_note: Extracted text interleaves this name and V-CRED-2's with the category label, then lists ten scores; the first five are assigned here by reading order. Independent check of the PDF layout puts 3 4 5 5 5 on the 'Social engineering*' line, confirming the pairing.
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing: LLM phishing and voice cloning scale social engineering.

name: Password brute-forcing and cracking
description: Guessing, spraying or offline cracking of passwords and weak keys to obtain legitimate credentials.
transcription_note: Second block of five scores after the interleaved names (see V-CRED-1); confirmed against the PDF layout.
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing; cracking stays compute-bound, so a smaller lift.

name: Exploitation of exposed credentials
description: Using credentials, tokens or keys leaked in code, logs, backups, breaches or misconfigured stores.
ai_shift_basis: Automated discovery of leaked secrets in code, logs and paste sites.

name: Expanding illegitimate access (e.g., escalating privileges)
description: Turning a foothold into broader access: privilege escalation, lateral movement, over-broad permissions abused to reach weight systems.
ai_shift_basis: Automated privilege-path discovery and escalation.

category_name: Undermining the Access Control System Itself
name: Encryption/authentication vulnerabilities (in the access control system)
description: Flaws in the cryptography or authentication protocols the access-control system relies on.
ai_shift_basis: Cryptanalysis is helped less than code review; implementation flaws more than design flaws.

category_name: Undermining the Access Control System Itself
name: Intentional backdoors in algorithms, protocols, or products (in the access control system)
description: Deliberately planted weaknesses in algorithms, protocols or products used for access control, e.g. subverted standards or vendors.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Backdoors are planted by states through standards and products; AI changes little.

category_name: Undermining the Access Control System Itself
name: Code vulnerabilities (in the access control system)
description: Implementation bugs in the access-control software itself that let an attacker bypass or forge authorisation.
ai_shift_basis: Code vulnerabilities in the access-control system: same uplift as other code.

category_name: Undermining the Access Control System Itself
name: Access to secret material undermining a protocol
description: Stealing signing keys, CA keys or other protocol secrets that let an attacker mint valid credentials or decrypt.
ai_shift_basis: Finding exposed secret material is partly automatable.

name: Incorrect configuration or security policy implementation
description: Misconfigurations, or policies written but never implemented, that leave sensitive systems or data reachable without defeating any control.
ai_shift_basis: Misconfiguration discovery is automated reconnaissance.

name: Additional (less secure) copies of sensitive data
description: Backups, checkpoints, research copies or discarded media holding weights that are less protected than the main copy.
ai_shift_basis: Automated enumeration finds stray copies faster.

name: Alternative (less secure) authentication or access schemes
description: Neglected secondary access paths: password recovery, break-glass, admin impersonation, management ports, legacy protocols.
ai_shift_basis: Alternative auth paths are found by reconnaissance, then still need a human or a credential.

name: Discovering existing vulnerabilities in the ML stack
description: Exploiting existing bugs in ML frameworks, serving stacks, GPU drivers or unsanitised model output to run code or read memory.
stage_note: Also a reach candidate (GPU-driver memory reads).
transcription_note: Category label 'Attack Vectors' is interleaved into the name lines at L1185; scores unaffected.
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing; AI finds ML-stack bugs as it finds other code bugs.

name: Intentional ML supply chain compromise
description: Deliberately compromising ML packages, tooling, accelerator hardware, annotations or models upstream (e.g. the torchtriton nightly compromise).
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing; malicious model artefacts and packages are cheap to generate.

name: Prompt-triggered code execution
description: Crafted prompts or inputs make a code-capable model execute attacker-chosen actions (prompt injection leading to code execution).
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing; injection payloads are optimised by models.

name: Model extraction
description: Inferring weights or parameters directly from many query responses, e.g. extracting embedding matrices through a normal API.
stage_note: Complete via the API: weights or parameters come out in the responses.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing, but what bounds extraction is how much each response leaks (logits, logprobs), which cleverness does not change; half a tier.

name: Model distillation
description: Training a model that mimics the target from its API outputs, replicating function without touching weights.
stage_note: Complete via the API, but yields a capability copy, not weights: shown on its own meter, not the headline.
ai_shift_basis: RAND flags it as rapidly changing; distillation is a machine-learning problem.

category_name: Nontrivial Access to Data or Networks
name: Digital access to air-gapped networks
description: Reaching and exfiltrating from isolated networks via removable media, covert channels, manipulated insiders or induced emergency connections.
stage_note: Also an exfil candidate: RAND's vector covers both penetrating and exfiltrating isolated networks.
ai_shift_basis: Bridging an air gap is mostly engineering and human access; modest lift.

category_name: Nontrivial Access to Data or Networks
name: Side-channel attacks (including through leaked emanations; i.e., TEMPEST attacks)
description: Inferring secrets from EM, power, acoustic, optical or cache/timing leakage; mostly useful for keys, not bulk weights.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Signal processing of emanations benefits from ML; the physics does not change.

category_name: Nontrivial Access to Data or Networks
name: Eavesdropping and wiretaps
description: Intercepting data in transit by tapping cables, links or network equipment, or by audio and RF bugs.
stage_note: A tap on a link carrying weights captures them in transit; retrieval is folded in.
ai_shift_basis: Wiretaps need physical access; AI helps only with the take.

name: Direct physical access to sensitive systems
description: Reaching sensitive hardware in person: tailgating, impersonation, maintenance or cleaning access, or retrieving undestroyed waste media.
ai_shift_basis: Physical access is bounded by people and places, not software.

name: Malicious placement of portable devices
description: Planting USB drives, malicious cables or peripherals for staff to connect, or rogue Wi-Fi access points.
ai_shift_basis: Device placement needs a person on site.

name: Physical access to devices in other locations
description: Compromising staff laptops and phones at homes, hotels, airports or other off-site locations.
ai_shift_basis: Physical access elsewhere needs a person.

name: Evasion of physical access control systems
description: Hacking or disabling the digital systems physical security depends on: cameras, alarms, badge readers, smart locks.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Evading physical access control is mostly tradecraft; some help with badge cloning.

name: Penetration of physical hardware security
description: Defeating tamper protection on HSMs, secure chips or enclosures by probing, fault injection or decapping.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Hardware probing is lab work; modest help with analysis.

name: Armed break-in
description: Forcible entry by armed personnel to seize hardware or data.
stage_note: Seizure carries the hardware out; reading the weights from it is still a reach step (V-X-2).
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: An armed break-in is people and planning.

name: Military takeover
description: A state's military force seizes the facility and everything in it.
stage_note: Seizure carries the hardware out; reading the weights from it is still a reach step (V-X-2).
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Military force is not lifted by AI in this model.
needs_government_note: Military takeover is met by a state, not a lab.

name: Services and equipment the organization uses
description: Compromised hardware, firmware, operating systems, IT and collaboration services, or CI/CD products the organisation uses (SolarWinds, CryptoAG).
ai_shift_basis: Hardware and service compromise is state logistics; software parts get some lift.

name: Code and infrastructure incorporated into the codebase
description: Malicious or vulnerable third-party packages, libraries, images and tooling built into the organisation's own software (xz backdoor, typosquats).
ai_shift_basis: Malicious code into dependencies is code, and generated at scale.

name: Vendors with access to information
description: Compromising vendors, contractors or service providers who hold access to the organisation's data or systems (OPM via subcontractor).
ai_shift_basis: Vendor access is about people and contracts.

name: Bribes and cooperation
description: Paying, persuading or deceiving insiders, including disgruntled or ideologically motivated staff, into acting for the adversary.
ai_shift_basis: Recruitment is human; AI helps targeting and OSINT.

name: Extortion
description: Coercing staff with threats to them or their families, or with leverage manufactured from small initial favours.
ai_shift_basis: Extortion is human; AI helps find leverage.

name: Candidate placement
description: Training and placing agents who are then hired into sensitive roles.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Placement is human; AI helps fabricate credentials.

name: Organizational leverage attacks
description: Building financial or legal leverage over the organisation, via investments or partnerships, to force or trick it into granting access.
transcription_note: One of nine vectors scored 1 at OC1-OC3 and >1 above. RAND's text (L1609) says eight; an independent check against the rand.org PDF confirms nine, so RAND's 'eight' is a slip in its prose (likely omitting military takeover). Scores stand as transcribed.
ai_shift_basis: Organisational leverage is money and influence.

name: Organizationally approved access
description: Leadership knowingly provides access, paid or legally compelled, often covertly.
stage_note: Not complete: sanctioned access still has to get past dual authorisation, split custody and egress controls (RAND SL5 irrecoverable-key policy targets exactly this).
ai_shift_basis: Sanctioned access is a decision, not a technique.
needs_government_note: Access approved by the organisation itself (including under legal compulsion) can only be overruled from outside it.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Self-exfiltration of its weights via permitted channels
ai_rationale: Terabyte transfers need multi-day planning and evasion; from AC3, unmetered research egress is little obstacle (cf. July 2026 throttling workarounds).
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: The model moves its own weight files out through channels it may use: artefact exports, code pushes, logs, uploads, API outputs.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Self-distilled data out via permitted channels
ai_rationale: Gigabytes leave easily, but a useful replica needs high-quality self-distillation and outside compute; only strong models manage both.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: The model generates training data or compressed know-how from which an outside party can train a capable replica; no weight access needed.
authored_basis: sl5_novel.txt:878-881 ("exfiltrate or distill the model weights")
stage_note: Yields a capability copy, not weights; kept in the AI-insider route because a distilled successor carries the model's goals.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Abuse of its own credentials or tooling
ai_rationale: Front-loaded: no exploit needed, agents already hold broad standing credentials, so only intent and planning limit it.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: The model uses credentials, service accounts and tools it legitimately holds beyond task scope: reading checkpoints, changing configs, launching jobs.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Sandbox escape via permitted egress
ai_rationale: July 2026: current-generation models escaped an eval sandbox through a package-proxy zero-day and reached the internet.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: The model exploits its execution environment (package proxy, container runtime, eval harness) to reach networks it should not, as in the July 2026 escape.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Covert and side channels
ai_rationale: Lagged: low bandwidth and hard to engineer reliably; matters once overt egress is capped or inspected, mostly for keys or coordination.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: Low-bandwidth leakage or coordination through steganography in outputs, timing, resource usage or EM modulation; suits keys and signals, not bulk weights.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Subverting oversight it helped build
ai_rationale: Ramp kept on purpose: undetected sabotage needs coding skill and a model of what reviewers miss, which grow together; no step change expected.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: Inserting subtle flaws into security code, monitors or research it writes; colluding with same-family monitors; sandbagging evaluations; tampering with results.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Unsanctioned workloads on lab compute
ai_rationale: Front-loaded: launching jobs is ordinary agent work; ordinary labs lack per-job attestation or security-grade quota accounting.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: Launching hidden training or inference jobs, or persistent copies of itself, on internal clusters: a rogue internal deployment that needs no exfiltration.
stage_note: Complete for the AI-insider route: the harm is a rogue internal deployment, nothing leaves.

category_name: The Lab's Own AI Model as Insider
name: Manipulating its operators
ai_rationale: Already non-zero: agentic-misalignment evaluations show coercive tactics in current models; reliable persuasion of trained staff needs more capability.
assumption_note: AUTHORED ASSUMPTION, not RAND: P(this step succeeds | a misaligned instance at this capability band attempts it) at a lab with ordinary security and no AI-specific controls; same 1-5 bins as RAND. Propensity to try is excluded.
description: Persuading, deceiving or pressuring staff into granting access, approving changes or relaxing controls on its behalf.

name: Standing insider access to weights
assumption_note: STRUCTURAL, not RAND: stands for 'nothing stops this stage' at an SL1-grade victim (p = 1.0 at every tier), so stage controls have something to act on. RAND scores entry/reach steps; Box 5.1 treats getting the weights out of an SL1 victim as given.
description: A cooperating insider uses access they already hold to read or copy weights; at SL1 many staff can.

name: Reading weights from hardware in hand
assumption_note: STRUCTURAL, not RAND: stands for 'nothing stops this stage' at an SL1-grade victim (p = 1.0 at every tier), so stage controls have something to act on. RAND scores entry/reach steps; Box 5.1 treats getting the weights out of an SL1 victim as given.
description: Someone at the machine reads weights from unencrypted disks, memory or interconnects.

name: Bulk network egress
assumption_note: STRUCTURAL, not RAND: stands for 'nothing stops this stage' at an SL1-grade victim (p = 1.0 at every tier), so stage controls have something to act on. RAND scores entry/reach steps; Box 5.1 treats getting the weights out of an SL1 victim as given.
description: Weights leave over the victim's own network links once reached; nothing meters or blocks outbound transfer at SL1.

name: Physical carry-out of media or devices
assumption_note: STRUCTURAL, not RAND: stands for 'nothing stops this stage' at an SL1-grade victim (p = 1.0 at every tier), so stage controls have something to act on. RAND scores entry/reach steps; Box 5.1 treats getting the weights out of an SL1 victim as given.
description: Weights leave on a drive, phone or implant carried out of the building.
